evidence_notes: All three evidence references point to the same identity (zhaoyachao__zdh_web::CVE-2025-65897) — the pre-patch vulnerable code paths and the post-patch fix are clearly documented and consistent with the boundary.
Single-case coverage: the mechanism would be stronger if at least one additional representative case from a different project demonstrated the same source→sink→fix pattern.
The fix commit (b2423378) shows a clean, reusable mitigation: Paths.get(fileName).getFileName().toString() — this is a strong signal for mechanism extraction.
main_issue: The mechanism is internally coherent — source shape (MultipartFile.getOriginalFilename), sink (filesystem path concatenation + write), missing guard (no basename normalization), and safe fix (centralized basename extraction) are all well-aligned. However, the boundary is demonstrated by a single representative case from one product (zdh_web), which limits confidence in cross-project generalizability. The reviewer notes correctly distinguish this from static-resource path traversal and archive traversal.
mechanism_name: multipart original filename used in server-side file path without basename normalization

evidence_notes: Pre-patch code (9ab5f77) at FileStorage.saveStream lines 116-124 confirms IOUtils.copyLarge with no size limit.
Fix commit (42b6c00) adds ServerConfig.getFileStorageMaxFileSize and size-bounded copy with partial-file cleanup.
No evidence of path traversal, archive escape, or path containment failure in source or patch.
main_issue: Well-defined boundary row. The mechanism (unbounded file upload causing storage exhaustion) is coherent: source shape (FileStorage.saveStream writing InputStream to FileDescriptor), sink (disk consumption), missing guard (no max bytes before IOUtils.copyLarge), exploit precondition (large upload exhausts disk), and safe fix (configured max, truncate, delete partial, error) are all internally consistent. Pre-patch and post-patch evidence from commit diffs confirms the mechanism is about upload size, not path containment. The mark_out_of_scope decision is sound — this should not be counted as path traversal recall.
mechanism_name: unbounded file upload size causes storage exhaustion

evidence_notes: Pre-patch code at 9e42d565a14f confirms copyFrom uses Selectors.SELECT_ALL for folder sources and moveToFolder moves source folders into destination without ancestor checks.
Fix commit fca7dc9c8348 adds checkSourceIsNotParent comparing resolved FileObject identities and walking getParent() upward before both moveTo and copyFrom.
Public advisory confirms the impact: copying a parent directory into /temp/ exposes files the user should not access, affecting all users including low-privilege DataShield users.
main_issue: Single representative case limits coverage confidence, but the mechanism is narrow, well-defined, and thoroughly evidenced: source shape (FilesResource.updateFile dispatching copy/move), sink (Selectors.SELECT_ALL recursive copy into descendant path), missing guard (no ancestor check before moveTo/copyFrom), exploit precondition (authenticated user places parent into child), and safe fix (checkSourceIsNotParent walking getParent() upward) are all coherent and derived from the same codebase. The guideline text is specific enough to generalize to other systems with recursive copy/move APIs lacking ancestor guards.
mechanism_name: recursive copy or move allows source folder to be placed under itself without ancestor guard

evidence_notes: Both cases provide pre-patch and fix-commit evidence with line-level references. OpenHAB CVE-2024-42468: CometVisuServlet.getRequestedFile constructs File objects from decoded pathInfo without canonical containment; fix adds canonical path prefix check. Solon CVE-2025-1584: StaticMappings.find strips prefix and calls repository.find without rejecting /../; fix adds contains('/../') guard. Evidence is sufficient and consistent with the claimed mechanism.

The mechanism boundary is narrow enough to be actionable: both fixes apply containment validation at the same point in the flow (after path resolution, before serving). The reviewer notes correctly exclude related but distinct patterns like upload filename traversal.
main_issue: The two cases share the same mechanism core: an HTTP request path enters a static-resource resolver, the path is decoded/transformed, and the resolved resource is served without verifying containment within the intended root. Implementation details differ (OpenHAB uses java.io.File canonicalization; Solon uses string prefix matching and repository.find), but the semantic mechanism is coherent. The reviewer notes appropriately scope to static-resource request path resolution, excluding upload filename traversal, archive extraction, and recursive copy/move patterns.
mechanism_name: static resource request path traversal without final containment guard
